title: The inbound metric that read zero for three days: a field-name mismatch
symptom: A production agent ran for days on an inbound metric that read zero. 410 of 410 log lines attributed the commenter to 'unknown'.
root_cause: One component normalized the commenter field under a different key than the one the consumer read, so every lookup silently missed.
fix: Align the read path with the canonical field name so the metric sees the data the client already normalizes.
real_numbers: 410/410 log lines said 'unknown'; the metric read 0 while the agent kept operating.

title: The agent that was blind to nested replies
symptom: Reply matching produced 0 matches over 1,035 inspected comments: every threaded response was invisible.
root_cause: The fetch returned only top-level comments while the API nests replies inside their parent, so the matcher never saw them.
fix: Flatten nested replies recursively preserving parent ids, and apply the same parent extraction to follow-up matching, depth guards and thread depth computation.
real_numbers: 1,035 comments inspected; 0 replies matched before the fix.

title: Legitimate 404s that kept opening the circuit breaker
symptom: The client kept failing under normal operation: 247 circuit breaker openings in a single day.
root_cause: Every 4xx counted as a circuit failure, but 404s are produced by design when probing for already-deleted comments; a handful of deletions tripped the breaker and killed unrelated reads and writes.
fix: Stop counting 400/404/409/410/422 against the breaker; keep counting 401/403/5xx.
real_numbers: 247 breaker openings in one day; 5 deleted comments could open the breaker.

title: The 85-minute cycle caused by one post with 316 comments
symptom: Cycles ran 85 minutes and stopped gracefully without answering anyone; the feed and follow-ups never ran.
root_cause: A single post with 316 comments consumed the entire per-cycle budget sequentially.
fix: Cap work per post per cycle at 10 comments, prioritize watchlist then recency, carry the remainder to the next cycle, and keep the full comment list for depth, history and dedup.
real_numbers: 316 comments on one post led to 85 min cycles; cap is now 10 comments/post/cycle.

title: The posts beyond #10 that were never reviewed
symptom: Posts 11+ were never revisited: new unanswered comments waited behind old ones and the daily reply budget went unused.
root_cause: The own-posts fetch window stopped at 10 and the global queue was processed post by post, oldest first, so newer comments starved.
fix: Fetch 30 own posts, order the global queue by watchlist and comment recency instead of post order, and raise the daily cap from 300 to 400.
real_numbers: Fetch window 10->30 posts; daily cap 300->400; the rate limiter allows ~570 writes.

title: The configured value that silently became the default: 12 became 6
symptom: A daily limit configured at 12 ran at the default 6, with no error anywhere.
root_cause: The validator clamped the value to an upper bound of 10 and then, outside the accepted range, replaced it with the default in silence.
fix: Accept the platform's real ceiling as the valid range so the configured value survives validation.
real_numbers: Configured 12 -> clamped to 10 -> silently fell back to default 6.

title: The pacing rule that left 4 of 12 publishing slots empty
symptom: With a 12 posts/day budget, 4 daily publishing slots were never used.
root_cause: A 2-hour minimum between posts was tuned for a lower daily rate; at 12 posts/day the pacing floor alone consumed the entire window.
fix: Lower the pacing minimum to 1 hour so it matches the actual daily budget.
real_numbers: Pacing floor 2h->1h; 4 of 12 daily slots wasted.

title: The fixed 3 posts per cycle that left ~218 comments unattended
symptom: Roughly 218 comments accumulated without replies because the reply pass stopped after 3 posts per cycle.
root_cause: The per-cycle post budget was hardcoded at 3 regardless of how many posts had pending comments.
fix: Make posts-per-cycle configurable and raise it to 6; raise the daily comment budget from 50 to 80.
real_numbers: Posts per cycle 3->6; ~218 comments left unattended; daily budget 50->80.

title: The self-optimizer that cut its own daily budget from 80 to 30
symptom: The agent's self-improvement pipeline flagged low-value replies, cut its own daily comment budget, then kept trying to cut it again cycle after cycle.
root_cause: The auto-applier measured reply quality on a rolling 50-reply window, interpreted clarification-heavy samples as overproduction, and applied budget cuts to itself; the same cut was then re-proposed repeatedly once blocked.
fix: Restrict the auto-applier to an allowlist of parameters so it cannot shrink its own daily budget, and cooldown per parameter to prevent oscillation.
real_numbers: Daily comment budget cut 80->30 comments/day; after the parameter was removed from the auto-apply allowlist, the same cut was re-proposed and rejected 4 more times, with the optimizer's own low-value estimate escalating 9/50 -> 18/50 -> 27/50 -> 24/50.
